newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam police minister says tougher measures needed.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam police minister says tougher measures needed.

text.p: Vietnam's new Interior Minister, Lieutenant-General Le Minh Huong, said on Monday tougher measures were needed to deal with growing problems from drug abuse to sex crimes and corruption.
In an interview during a break in proceedings at the National Assembly, Huong said Vietnam was being confronted with many new difficulties.

"As you can see, now there are big problems such as rape, child sexual abuse and drug abuse in schools," he said. "I think all developing countries face such problems, but it's become very serious and we have to get over this."
His talk with foreign reporters on Monday amounted to an unusual effort at openness by the head of a traditionally secretive government department charged with maintaining internal security.

Huong, who is also a member of the elite Politburo, was appointed as Interior Minister in a cabinet reshuffle last week. But he is widely reported to have been in effective charge of the powerful police ministry since a landmark Communist Party Congress in late June.
His predecessor, Bui Thien Ngo, who resigned at around the time of the party congress, is not known to have spoken directly to foreign journalists during his tenure.
Huong said Vietnam's younger generation was particularly vulnerable, adding that special emphasis was needed to combat growing problems with illegal narcotics.
"The young generation is the generation that will build the country, and we should educate them to make them understand how dangerous drug-abuse is," he said.
"Also we should apply very strict legal action against drug-traffickers and drug-related crimes."
Huong emphasised that while Hanoi had announced a number of measures in recent months aimed at tightening security controls these were not intended to frighten foreign businesspeople and investors.
"Our aim is to keep the country stable and also the development of the country stable. Any country will be concerned about their security," he said, adding in English: "You (foreigners) are welcome."
